title: hydo results, version 1
description: Any version-1 record or document (the schema's root).

Run.description:
One run of one schedule: `result.json` of `hydo run`, and every run of an exploration in
`events.jsonl`.

hydo_version.description: The hydo that wrote the document (documents only).

epoch.description:
The fingerprint epoch of that hydo (documents only; added in M155): fingerprints of one
epoch are comparable, across epochs only verdicts are. Absent: before M155, epoch 1.

tag.description: The explorer's name for the run (`seed-3`, `repro-3`, `shrink-1-0`, `min-a`, ...).

seed.description: The exploration seed (or sweep point number) the run belongs to.

role.description: Why the explorer made the run ([`role`]).

schedule.description: The schedule, in the schedule language (`disk=cut | run C=12`).

class.description: The explorer's finding class of the schedule (`durable-defaults`, `unsafe-knob`, ...).

image.description: Documents only: in a stream, the [`Start`] record names the image.

engine.description: Documents only: in a stream, the [`Start`] record names the engine.

findings.description:
What the run checked: failed invariants and assertions, every history check, every
error kind.

properties.description: Documents only: the run's property table.

secs.description: The run's wall time in seconds (engine side).

worker.description: The explorer worker that ran it.

control.description: Runs on agent images: the control transcript of each conversation (added in M120).

warnings.description:
Why a passing run may have checked nothing (added after 0.1.0): the workload acknowledged
nothing, or a history check judged an empty history. One sentence each; absent when
there is none. A run with warnings still passed: the verdict is unchanged.

diagnosis.description:
Why the run failed, when it did not pass (added in M178): what the run's own files say
and, when collected, what a replay of the run read in the guest at the stop where the
verdict was given. `hydo run` writes it; the fingerprints never depend on it.

messages.description:
Each `type: messages` check of the run (added after 0.2.0, docs/design/messaging.md):
its declaration, each claim's status and the measures of the history. Each claim is also
a `history-check` finding, under the id `<check>.<claim>`.

path.description: The image as it was given (a path, or an explorer image name).

resolved.description: The path the engine opened, when it differs from `path`.

epoch.description:
The fingerprint epoch of the hydo that built the image (its `/etc/hydo/image.json`, added
in M155; absent for an image built before).

kernel.description:
The guest kernel the image names (its record), as `<file> (Linux <version>, sha256 <hex>)`
(added in M155).

built_by.description: The hydo that built the image, from the build record next to it (`<image>.json`, M155).

manifest_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the manifest the image was built from (the build record, M155).

services.description: The Docker/OCI images of its services with their digests (the build record, M155).

BuiltBy.description: The hydo that built an image (added in M155).

ServiceImage.description: A service built from a Docker/OCI image (added in M155).

image.description: The image as the manifest gives it.

Engine.description: The engine and the machine it gave the guest.

backend.description: `hvx` (the Linux kernel module), `hvm` (Hypervisor.framework on the Mac) or `kvm` (stock Linux KVM).

args.description: The options passed to the engine (`--ram-mib`, `--vcpus`, `--cpu`).

guest_kernel.description: hvm: the guest kernel and the first 16 hex digits of its SHA-256.

text.description: The verdict line (the guest's `HYDO-ORACLE: ...`, or what the host made of it).

guest.description: The guest's own verdict, when the host's history checks replaced it.

before_error_logs.description: The verdict before the error logs failed the run (`unknown: fail`).

Fingerprints.description: A run's fingerprints: equal fingerprints mean bit-identical runs.

fp.description: The whole run (console, snapshot, guest RAM, disk).

ctl.description:
An agent image's run: the hash of its control transcripts (`ctl=` on the RESULT line,
M126): equal hashes mean the host typed the same commands at the same stops.

Finding.description: What a run checked, in one shape for every source.

id.description:
The property id, the check id, the invariant's id (or the verdict's signature), or the
error kind's signature.

details.description: What the source says beyond that (the examples show each source's fields).

PropertyTable.description: The property table: every assertion property over a set of runs (hydo/ASSERTIONS.md).

setup_complete_runs.description: Of those, runs that printed HYDO-SETUP-COMPLETE.

violations.description: Properties whose verdict is a FAIL.

Property.description: One property over the runs of a table.

declared.description: Declared in a HYDO-ASSERT-DECL record (the catalog).

passes.description: Evaluations that held, and that did not.

runs_passed.description: Runs with at least one such evaluation.

verdict.description:
The table's verdict (`PASS`, `FAIL`, `FAIL (never evaluated)`, `FAIL (reached)`,
`FAIL (deadline missed)`, `NOT EXERCISED`, `NOT EVALUATED`).

first_failure.description: The details of the first failing evaluation, as the record wrote them.

slowest_ok_s.description: Eventually properties: the slowest episode that held, in seconds.

within_s.description:
Eventually properties: the deadline in seconds after the anchor (the records' `within_s`,
the largest seen; added after M176).

ErrorLogs.description: A run's error-log analysis (`errors:` in the manifest).

unknown.description: `report` or `fail`: what a new kind does to the run.

steps.description: The workload's steps (the labels of where a line was written refer to them).

boots.description: The guest's HYDO-ERRLOG-SUM record of every boot.

truncated.description: A boot printed only its first kinds (`errors.max`).

tjk.description: Tick jitter: the first and last delayed tick.

pctf.description: PCT points that fired, and the window.

count.description: Packets of the stream in that step (absent: the freeze never fired).

reused.description: Taken from an earlier sweep (`--fc-traces`), not run.

ShrinkStep.description: A shrink candidate's place in its shrink.

of.description: The signature being shrunk (a failure's, or an error kind's).

kept.description: The candidate kept the failure and became the next round's schedule.

Artifacts.description: Files of a run, relative to the document's directory.

consoles.description: The guest consoles: the run's, then the recovery boot's after a power cut.

Control.description:
The control transcript of one conversation of a run on an agent image (added in M120,
docs/design/guest-control.md "The control transcript"): which controller decided, the
engine's stop cadence, the transcript's hash and where the transcript file is. A run has one
per conversation (the run; after a power cut also the recovery boot).

controller.description: The controller that decided (`schedule`), or `replay` for a transcript typed again.

hash.description: The transcript's hash, 16 hex digits (`ctl=` on the RESULT line).

stops.description: Stops at which the host acted.

transcript.description:
The transcript file (`control.jsonl`, `control.recovery.jsonl`), relative to the
document's directory.

Diagnosis.description:
Why a run failed (added in M178; `result.json`'s `diagnosis`, `hydo inspect diagnose`).

`failure` names what failed (an open set): `service-exited` (a service's process ended
while it started), `service-not-ready` (its readiness check did not pass in time),
`service-setup`, `provision`, `restart` (a service did not come back after the faults),
`mount`, `timeout` (a phase ran out of time), `vm` (the guest or the engine stopped),
`control`, `violation` (a check failed; no process failed) or `other`.

summary.description: One or two sentences for a reader who sees nothing else.

verdict_at.description: The stop where the verdict was given (`hydo inspect start <run dir> --at end` looks there).

process.description: The process whose end caused the failure.

exits.description: Every process the host started that ended before the verdict with a status other than 0.

likely.description: Conclusions drawn from the facts, each with its reason.

kernel.description:
The kernel's lines about crashes and memory (out of memory, segfault, panic), from the
console and, when collected, from `dmesg`.

evidence_status.description:
`collected` (a replay read `evidence` in the guest), `not-collected` (with the reason in
`evidence_note`) or `failed`.

next.description: Commands that look further, exactly as they can be run.

RunPoint.description:
Where in a run something is (added in M178): its conversation (`boot`, `run`, `recovery`),
the number of the stop (the control transcript's `n`) and the engine's virtual clock there
(hvx's instruction clock, hvm's and kvm's exit count). `point` is the two in the form
`hydo inspect start --at` takes (`boot:172`).

ProcessEnd.description:
How a process the host started ended (added in M178): the agent's `exit` (a service, the
provisioning) or `done` (a command) event.

handle.description:
The service's or the command's name as the host started it (`redis`, `provision`,
`setup:redis`, `workload`).

status.description: The exit status as a shell reports it (the code, or 128 + the signal).

signal_by_hydo.description:
The host sent that signal itself (a kill of the schedule, the end of a check). False: a
signal hydo did not send (for SIGKILL usually the kernel's out-of-memory killer).

output.description: What the agent kept of its output (commands only).

at.description: Where it ended (the first recorded stop by which the host had seen the event).

ProbeEnd.description: A readiness check's end (added in M178).

why.description: `ok`, `deadline` (it did not pass in time) or `died` (the service's process ended first).

deadline_s.description: The time limit, in seconds of guest time.

Evidence.description: Text read in the guest (added in M178): a log's tail, a command's output.

what.description: What it is, in words (`the log of redis`, `the kernel's messages`).

source.description: The file read, or the command run.

text.description: The text (invalid UTF-8 replaced by U+FFFD).

bytes.description: The whole size in bytes (of the file, or of the command's output).

truncated.description: Only the end (a log) or the start (a command's output) of it is in `text`.

MessagesCheck.description:
One `type: messages` check of a run: what the project declared its system promises, what
held, and what was measured.

declaration.description:
The declaration with every default filled in (the claims, `acknowledgement`,
`retention_ms`, `clock_steps`, the measures' options).

claims.description: Each claim the declaration makes, in the order reported (`no-phantom` first).

ops.description: The history's operations and drained records.

warnings.description: Records the checker could not read, claims that judged nothing.

error.description:
Why the declaration could not be checked (a key this hydo does not know); then there are
no claims and no measures.

judged.description: Candidates judged (messages, pairs or deliveries, by claim).

undecided.description: Candidates the history could not decide (a clock step inside, two boots, no time).

summary.description: One sentence; a violation's names its witness.

MessageMeasures.description:
The measures of a messages history (every one optional: a measure added later is an
addition). Durations are guest milliseconds between records of one boot.

sends.description:
Send items invoked, and their outcomes; `recovered`: messages whose sends were all
unknown and that were delivered.

lost.description: Acknowledged messages never delivered to a drained group that had to receive them.

excused.description:
Missing messages excused, by reason (`expired`, `dead-lettered`, `possibly-consumed`,
`rejected`) and those `undecided` (across a power cut).

aborted.description: Deliveries of messages whose every send failed.

stored_copies.description: Messages with more than one system id.

processing.description: Messages with accepted acknowledgements of two deliveries in one group.

group_overlap.description: Messages two members of a group surely held at once.

reorders.description: Per group with any: first deliveries against the order of the sends.

held.description: From a receive's completion to its delivery's acknowledgement's completion.

invisible.description:
Deliveries not acknowledged that came back: the time until (`ms`) and its ratio to the
declared lease (`lease_ratio`).

unseen.description: Acknowledged messages never delivered to some group that had to receive them.

across_boots.description: Durations left out because their records are in two boots.

messages.description: (message, group) pairs delivered at least once.

inverted_pairs.description: Pairs whose sends were ordered and whose first deliveries were not.

max_distance.description: The most messages that followed one message and were first delivered before it.

epoch.description: The fingerprint epoch of that hydo (added in M155; absent: before M155, epoch 1).

freeze_sweep.description: `--sweep freeze`: the trace and adaptive stages (their counts, centres, windows, rounds).

failures.description: Every failing first run, in seed order.

shrinks.description: One minimal schedule per class and signature.

properties.description: Images whose guests emit HYDO-ASSERT records.

Config.description: How the exploration was asked for.

strategy.description: The strategy (`random`, `swarm`, `process`, ...), or `sweep:<kind>` for a sweep.

branch_marker.description: `--branch`: the marker the runs branch at, and the variants per branch point.

schedule.description: `--schedule`: the one schedule given by hand.

Summary.description: The numbers of an exploration. Absent fields do not apply to its mode.

branch_points.description:
Branch explorations: branch points found, runs made, timing variants per point and the
tick-jitter permille.

reproduced.description: Failures whose every re-run gave the same fingerprint.

reproduced_standalone.description:
Branch explorations: failures reproduced as plain schedules, and failures that need the
timing change.

quiet_wait_s.description: Seconds the pool waited for `$HYDO_QUIET_FILE` to go away.

error_kinds_new.description: Error kinds new in some run, and runs with a new kind.

vacuous_passes.description:
First runs that passed with a warning that they may have checked nothing (their run
records' `warnings`; added after 0.1.0).

Failure.description: A failing run of an exploration and its re-runs.

signature.description: The grouping key: the verdict with numbers as `#` (violations: up to ` order=`).

reproduced.description: Every re-run gave the run's fingerprint.

timing_only.description: Branch explorations: the failure appears only with the timing change.

Reproduction.description: A run of a schedule again, to confirm it.

fp.description: Absent: the run gave no result.

present.description: Error kinds: the kind was present in this run.

Shrink.description: A failure shrunk to a minimal schedule (one per class and signature).

verdict.description: The verdict the minimal schedule kept during the shrink.

tries.description: Shrink candidates run (every candidate of a round counts).

min_class.description: The minimal schedule's own finding class.

min_verdict.description: The verdict of the first confirmation run.

identical.description: The two confirmations gave the same fingerprint.

repro_command.description: The command line that runs the minimal schedule once.

composition.description: Test composer: the composition of the minimal `W=` in words.

commands.description: Test composer: the command ids of the plan.

contents.description: Test composer: each used command's content hash.

stable.description: Test composer: the resolved `W=:` form (commands by id).

stable_schedule.description: Test composer: the schedule with the resolved form (or `W=@<key>`).

stable_note.description: Test composer: why the minimal schedule keeps the seed form.

ErrorKinds.description: The error kinds of an exploration.

ErrorKind.description: One error kind over an exploration.

signature.description: The first 12 hex digits of sha256("<service>\n<template>").

template.description: The line with its times, numbers, ids and client ports blanked.

new.description: New in at least one run (the known list did not cover it).

runs.description: Runs that had it, and runs in which it was new.

seeds.description: The first 12 seeds that had it.

lines.description: Lines of this kind over every run.

reason.description: The reason of the known-list entry that covered it.

FirstNew.description: An error kind's first run in which it was new.

ErrorShrink.description: A new error kind shrunk to the smallest schedule that still writes it.

Liveness.description: One eventually property over an exploration.

held_runs.description: Runs in which every episode held in time, and runs with a missed deadline.

slowest_s.description: The slowest run that held: its time and its run (tag).

first_miss_run.description: The first run with a missed deadline, and that episode's details.

within_s.description:
The property's deadline in seconds after its anchor (the records' `within_s`; the largest
when runs differ), so that `slowest_s` can be read against it (added after M176).

slowest_late_s.description:
The slowest episode that held only after its deadline (the host's `satisfied only <t>s
after ...`): the guest time the property needed in that run, and the run (added after
M176). A deadline of at least this would have held there.

ExplorationArtifacts.description: Where an exploration's files are, relative to its directory.

consoles.description: The directory of the guest consoles (`<tag>.log`, `<tag>.recovery.log`).

Start.description: The first record of an exploration's stream.

epoch.description: The fingerprint epoch of that hydo (added in M155; absent: before M155, epoch 1).

End.description: The last record of an exploration's stream: the exploration finished.

Diff.description:
`diff.json`: where two runs first differ (`hydo diff`, `hydo explain`; added in M165). The
runs are aligned event by event, per conversation (the control transcripts' commands, notes
and reports, and the guest's console lines); `first` is the first event that differs,
`timing` the first shared event the two runs reach at another stop or guest time, and
`first_outcome` the first difference in what the checks judge (acknowledged lists,
assertions, history records, verdicts) among records both runs write.

neighbour.description: `hydo explain`: how run B's schedule was made from run A's (`without K=redis@11+1`).

identical.description: No difference at the levels compared.

one_sided.description:
Records of a kind the other run never writes (an assertion id it never reports), each at
its first occurrence: often code only one of two images has.

counts.description: Every difference, counted by conversation and level.

hunks.description: The number of separate places where the runs differ.

DiffSide.description: One of the two runs of a diff (added in M165).

Divergence.description: A place where two runs part (added in M165).

level.description: The level of its first differing event (`timing` for a guest-time divergence).

a.description:
Where it is in run A and in run B (the first differing event, or, on the side that has
none, the next shared event).

context.description: The events both runs share right before it, oldest first.

lines.description: The differing events: those only A has (`a` set) and those only B has (`b` set).

details.description: What differs inside two events of the same kind (`only in B: 11`, `env: only in A: ...`).

DiffPoint.description:
Where an event of one run is in that run (added in M165): its conversation, the number of the
stop that saw it (the control transcript's `n`) and the engine's virtual clock at it (hvx's
instruction clock, hvm's exit count).

DiffLine.description:
One event of a diff (added in M165): its level, its text, and where it is in each run (absent
on the side that does not have it).

level.description:
`control` (a command the host typed, an engine action), `controller` (the host
controller's notes and reports), `guest` (a line the guest printed), `assertion`,
`assertion-decl`, `history`, `fake-world`, `error-log`, `composer`, `outcome` (the
acknowledged and failed lists, the end of a conversation) or `verdict`.

after.description:
The host controller's last note before it in the run that has it (`hydo-ob: KILLED redis
before step 11`): where in the workload it happened.

DiffCount.description: How many events of one level one run has and the other does not (added in M165).

DiagnosisDoc.description: `hydo inspect diagnose <run dir>`: a run's [`Diagnosis`] as a document (added in M178).

Timeline.description:
`hydo inspect events <run dir>`: a run's events with their stops, filtered and paged (added in
M178).

offset.description: The index of the first event shown among them.

truncated.description: More events match than are shown.

next.description: The command that shows the next page.

TimelineConversation.description: One conversation of a run in its timeline (added in M178).

end.description: How it ended (`end at snapshot S1`, `end: HYDO-ORACLE: OK ...`, `power cut`).

snapshots.description:
Whether `hydo inspect` can keep a snapshot at its stops (boot and the workload; not after
the workload's end, not in a recovery boot, not under timing schedules) or works on one
live branch there.

TimelineEvent.description: One event of a run's timeline (added in M178).

point.description:
`<conversation>:<stop>`, the form `hydo inspect start --at` takes; absent for the run's
result.

at.description: The engine's virtual clock at the stop.

kind.description:
An open set: `command` (the host typed an agent command), `exit` (a process the host
started ended), `probe` (a readiness check ended), `done` (a command ended), `fault` (a
fault applied or healed), `note` (the host controller's note), `report` (a line of the
run's report), `assertion`, `guest` (a line the guest printed), `snapshot`, `engine`,
`end` (the end of a conversation), `verdict`.

details.description: The record behind it (an agent event, a command).

Inspect.description: One answer of `hydo inspect` (added in M178): `op` says which; the members of that op are set.

at.description:
The state the call saw: the session's stop (`snapshot`), or the branch after the earlier
calls (`live`).

notes.description: Remarks for the caller (what the state is, what to try next).

at.description:
The stop the session looks at, and how: `snapshot` (every call starts from the stop's
snapshot, so each sees the same state) or `live` (calls run one after another on one
branch from the stop; each sees what the earlier ones left).

idle_timeout_s.description: It ends by itself after this many seconds without a call.

frozen.description: Every process was stopped (SIGSTOP) at the stop (`--freeze`).

InspectExec.description: A command run in the guest by `hydo inspect` (added in M178).

service.description: The service whose network namespace it ran in.

status.description: The exit status (the code, or 128 + the signal).

timed_out.description: Its time limit (`--timeout`, guest time) ended it.

InspectText.description: Text read from the guest by `hydo inspect` (added in M178).

text.description: The text (invalid UTF-8 replaced by U+FFFD), absent when `hex` is given.

hex.description: The bytes in lower-case hex, when they are not UTF-8 text.

truncated.description: Fewer bytes are shown than there are (`--max-bytes`).

InspectEntry.description: A file or directory entry (added in M178).

InspectProcess.description: A process in the guest (added in M178).

state.description: The kernel's state letter (`R`, `S`, `D`, `T` stopped, `Z` zombie).

InspectSocket.description: A socket in the guest (added in M178).

InspectCost.description: What a call cost (added in M178).

stops.description: Engine stops the call took (a replay to the stop counts every stop of it).

InspectError.description: A call of `hydo inspect` that failed (added in M178): what was wrong and what would work.

try.description: Commands that would work, exactly as they can be run.
